findings.claim: TRUNK-6682 carries the `backport` label, but the new API is tagged only `@since 3.0.0` (DataWithMetadata:21, StorageService.getDataWithMetadata, the 3-arg injectMissingMetadata, @Deprecated(since="3.0.0")), and the code uses Java 16+ syntax, a record at ImageHandler.java:153 and pattern-matching instanceof at S3StorageService.java:178, which a Java 8 maintenance build rejects; which lines does this backport to? If 2.8.x is one, @since needs those versions and those two constructs need to become a plain class and a cast. This is the surviving half of the earlier @since thread (r4070873955: 'plus whatever maintenance lines it gets backported to').
findings.evidence: Ticket JSON labels include 'backport'. StorageService/LocalStorageService/ObjectMetadata carry '@since 2.8.0, 2.7.5, 2.6.16, 2.5.15' (multi-line convention); new members say only 3.0.0. `git show a085b50b6~1:pom.xml` (last 2.8.0-SNAPSHOT commit before the 3.0.0 bump) has <javaCompilerVersion>1.8</javaCompilerVersion>; Java 21 arrived on master later (5f300cfaf/80f3454b0, 2025-07-22/25). `javac --release 8` on a file with a private record and `o instanceof String s` fails: 'records are not supported in -source 8', 'pattern matching in instanceof is not supported in -source 8'; the cast form compiles. Master's versions of the storage/handler files use no Java 9+ syntax (grep), consistent with keeping them backportable. Author converted DataWithMetadata from record to class in 956bc83f9 but left LoadedImage a record.

findings.claim: Reads of legacy-layout obs (valueComplex holding a bare name that parseDataKey prefixes with the obs dir) gain nothing: they still cost 6 filesystem calls with 3 Files.exists plus a failed stat, the same total as master, while new-layout reads drop from 6 to 3 with one exists; TRUNK-6682's 'at most one existence-related check' and the description's '5 → 3' hold only for the new layout, so does the ticket stay open for legacy reads? Follow-up to the unanswered thread r4070873940 on AbstractHandlerTest.
findings.evidence: Throwaway JUnit test (deleted) intercepting java.nio.file.Files with Mockito.mockStatic(CALLS real method, recording names), driving AbstractHandler.getObs on a real LocalStorageService. Controls: one Files.exists call recorded exactly [exists], empty runnable recorded []. PR head: new-layout [exists, readAttributes, newInputStream]; legacy-layout [exists(storage/<bare>%2Etxt), exists(appdata/<bare>), readAttributes(storage/obs/<bare>%2Etxt) -> fails, exists(appdata/obs/<bare>), readAttributes, newInputStream]. Master (api/src checked out from master, then restored with git checkout HEAD -- api/src): new-layout 4x exists + newInputStream + readAttributes; legacy-layout 4x exists + newInputStream + readAttributes. Legacy data read correctly on both ('legacy', len=6).

verdict: Close to mergeable: the prior review rounds' findings are fixed at the head and the targeted tests pass, but whether this backports (it uses Java 16+ syntax and @since 3.0.0 only, against a 'backport' ticket) and whether TRUNK-6682 covers legacy-layout reads, which are unchanged at 6 filesystem calls, need answers first.
